# Decisions: record-citations

- 2026-08-09T08:16:45.007Z — rule: **§ cites a section of a HAND-WRITTEN document only (docs/SPEC.md, docs/FORMAT.md, CLAUDE.md), named verbatim and whole, kept on one line, and closed by comma or parens whenever the next word could read as part of the heading. Tasks, phases and decisions are cited by id, never with §.** — chose **ONE citation grammar, fixed by convention rather than tooling. § points only into hand-written documents and names a `##`/`###` heading or a `**Bold label**` sub-section VERBATIM AND WHOLE; sub-parts are locators AFTER a comma (`§Acceptance criteria, Phase 4`, `§State, task_files`, `§CLI UI, color law`), never part of the § name; the citation never straddles a line break. Tasks, phases and decisions carry their own ids and are cited bare: `record-index 4.2`, `cross-initiative-conflicts 2.2`, `speed T2`, `Phase 3 — Contract + proof`, `D17`, `felt-cost D3`. Written into CLAUDE.md as `### Citing things (the § rule)`; all 15 broken refs in hand-written docs and all 46 in source comments fixed in the same change.** over Banning § from the record entirely in favour of `SPEC > Derived index`; allowing § to point at plan.md/decisions.md headings on the grounds that those ARE real markdown headings; and shipping a `sofar doctor` detector to enforce resolution mechanically instead of by convention. because Measured first: 244 § refs in .sofar/, 386 repo-wide, and NO code anywhere parses the symbol (zero hits for the literal in packages/) — so this is a legibility contract with zero format risk, and history needed no migration. The symbol was never the problem. § is the standard section mark (RFCs, W3C, ISO) and 164 of the 244 record refs already resolved correctly, so BANNING it would have discarded the working majority to fix the broken minority. The damage was three mechanical classes, all of which defeat search while reading fine to a human: UNTERMINATED names (`§CLI and acceptance extended` — § opens a heading and nothing closes it, so extraction yields garbage like `§Envelope + decision + tests (stamps when config exists`); NICKNAMES that name no heading (`§Acceptance` where the heading is `## Acceptance criteria`, `§Envelope` for `## Event envelope` — CLAUDE.md itself committed this); and LINE-WRAPPED citations (`§Sync` / `client`, 5 of them) which are invisible even to a correct grep. GENERATED PROJECTIONS are excluded despite the strongest counter-argument: plan.md really does render phases as `## Phase 1 — Incremental core`, a genuine markdown heading. It is still wrong, because that file's first line reads "generated by sofar — do not hand-edit; truth lives in events.jsonl" — citing a projection's heading binds the reference to a rendering that projections/templates/ can change at any time, while the id in the event payload is truth and cannot. So the test is not "does the target have a heading" but "is the target hand-written". A DOCTOR DETECTOR was rejected for now on sequencing, not merit: it is the only thing that catches rename drift (rename `## CLI` in SPEC and ~30 citations go stale silently, exactly the failure this decision cannot prevent), but the convention has to exist before anything can enforce it, and it is new surface on a repo whose guard-rails say detection-only, never rewrite. Left untouched deliberately: docs/harness.md (21 broken refs) is marked "SUPERSEDED — do not update", and events.jsonl history is append-only by law, so its stale refs are historical fact rather than debt.
